headline: Frequently asked questions
lede: The questions we get most often, answered.

items.v: Yes, on most of the line

a: Yes, across most of the line, but not every club and not every loft, so here is the whole picture rather than a yes that turns into a no at checkout.

items.q: Will there be a left-handed blade putter?
a: Not today. The Tracer LGP01 Blade is right hand only.
The Tracer LGP02 Mallet is built in both hands, so if it is a Lucky putter you are after rather than specifically a blade, that one exists now.
We are not going to put a date on a left-handed blade here. When it is real it will be on the site with a price and a stock number like everything else.

items.q: I'm 5'9". Is a 35-inch putter right for me?
a: Both Tracers are built at 35 inches, and that is the only length we make today. We do not cut or extend one before it ships.

The useful comparison is the putter you already own: measure it heel to grip cap and see how far off 35 is. That number tells you more than your height does, because putter length follows how you stand over the ball.

If you want it shorter, a club fitter can do it after purchase, but read the returns page first. Cutting, bending or regripping a putter ends its return window, so it is a decision to make after the sixty days, not during them.

items.q: Can I get a different length, grip size or shaft?
a: No. Every club ships with the stock shaft and the stock grip, in one length, and there is no option to change any of it at checkout.
Grips are sold separately if you want to change one yourself. Fitting a new grip to the club counts as a modification, so it ends the return window on that club.

items.q: Which wedge loft should I start with?
a: Start from the wedge already in your bag rather than from a chart. The gap between your pitching wedge and your next club is the hole you are filling, and the Carver's loft ladder on the product page walks through it.
The 01 comes in six lofts from 50° to 60°, in two grinds. Which grind suits you is a separate question from which loft, and it has its own section on the product page.

items.q: Does the club come with a head cover?
a: No. No club in the line ships with a head cover: not the wedges, not the putters, not the hybrid.
Covers are sold separately: a blade cover, a mallet cover and a driver cover.

items.q: The white grip is going to get dirty, isn't it?
a: Grips are a consumable on any club and we sell replacements in several colours. Fitting one yourself ends the return window on the club, so if you are still inside your sixty days it is worth waiting.
Orders leave the warehouse in one to two business days, and ground delivery takes a few business days after that. You get a tracking number as soon as the carrier scans the parcel.
What shipping costs is worked out at checkout, before you pay.

items.q: Do you ship outside the US?
a: Yes, worldwide. The rate is calculated at checkout like any other, so you see it before you pay.

items.q: Tracking hasn't moved in days. Where is it?
a: Tracking updates on scans, so it moves in jumps. A day or two of silence in transit is normal and usually means the parcel is between two of them.
If there has been no movement for longer than that, email support@luckygolf.com with your order number and we will trace it.

items.q: The wrong loft turned up. What now?
a: That is a picking error rather than a return, and it does not come out of your sixty days.
Send the order number and a photo of the loft stamp on the sole (one picture settles it) and hold onto the club until we have replied.

items.q: How long do I have to send something back?
a: Sixty days on a club, thirty on apparel and gear, both counted from delivery. Customized items are final sale unless they arrive defective.

items.q: Can I actually hit it first?
a: A putter, yes. Use it, that is what sixty days is for. It has to come back unmarked, with no face marks, sole wear, scratches, dents, chips, bag chatter or grip wear.
A wedge, one per order, on a turf mat or another non-abrasive surface. Any others stay factory sealed, and the tested one comes back with no groove wear.
A hybrid, driver or wood has to appear completely unused.

items.q: Can I just post the club back?
a: No, and this is the one mistake that is hard to undo. Every club return needs approval and photo verification before it ships. A club that arrives without authorization is not accepted.
Email or chat first with the order number and photos of the face and the sole. It takes one message.

items.q: It's a gift. Does the window start when I give it?
a: No. The window runs from delivery, so a club bought in November and handed over at Christmas has spent most of its sixty days in a closet.
Tell us, with photos, and do not send it anywhere until we have answered. A club that fails in normal use is a different conversation from one you have decided against.
What is settled: if the fault is ours, we pay the return shipping. Defective gear may be replaced or refunded after inspection, and a customized item is returnable if it arrives defective.
There is no lifetime warranty on a club. Sixty days is the written policy.
After it closes, a manufacturing fault depends on what the fault is. Send photos and we will tell you where we land, rather than guess at it here.
You do, on a change of mind, and the original shipping is not refunded. We do not send a prepaid label.
Where the fault is ours it should not work that way, but that case is not written down yet. See the question above.
